resolveTrade's per-deal `Market.update` (moves.js:455) is NOT carried into per-turn settlement. Market.update assigns `prev = prices` (js/market.js:70); calling it per settlement would flatten the trend arrow the market panel draws (market.js:81-86) in a deal-count-dependent way. Prices themselves cannot move from settlement — update reads Area GDP and population only (market.js:42-47, :58-74) and settlement moves treasuries. advanceTurn already calls it once per turn (world.js:1216).

steps.where: new file js/deals.js (classic IIFE global `Deals`, same shape as js/pacts.js:41-204); script tag immediately after pacts.js in index.html:101, dev.html:116, tests/run.html:106
steps.detail: Private state: `seq` (number), `deals` (array, ascending id), `offers` (array, ascending id), `pending` (array of deal ids awaiting the player's renegotiation answer), `ended` (array of {id, turn, reason} with reason in expired|lapsed|declined|party-gone|self-deal, capped to `nation.historyWindow`×2 like pacts.js:178-180). A `byId` Map index rebuilt on load and on every mutation. Exports: reset, serialize, loadState, offer, accept, decline, counter, cancel, tick(tune, rng), waiting(), answer(dealId, decision), forNation(nid), byId(id), active(), openOffers(), count(). World.js calls it behind `typeof Deals !== 'undefined'` like Pacts at world.js:1173 so the headless pages that omit it still run.

steps.step: Ids that reproduce from the seed
steps.detail: One monotonic `seq` for both instruments: offers get 'o'+(++seq), deals 'd'+(++seq); an accepted offer becomes a deal with a NEW id carrying `offerId` as provenance; a renewal keeps its id (A3's map links and ledger cross-references stay stable) and records a 'renewed' ledger entry. A caller cannot pass an id (overwrite after spread, ledger.js:82). Never Date.now, Math.random or a content hash — a hash of (turn, parties, resource) collides when both seats of a pair each propose the same resource in one round. Ids are issued only inside Moves.resolve paths (player click or AI.takeTurn ai.js:677-694, both in TurnSystem order) and inside Deals.tick, so two runs on one seed issue the same ids in the same order.

steps.step: Iteration order for settlement and expiry
steps.detail: All per-turn passes walk `deals` ascending by numeric id — never a plain object keyed by nation id (JS enumerates integer-like keys such as '48' before '06' and 'n1', so the order would depend on which nations exist). Per deal, a fixed op order (buyer Game.spend then seller Game.earn, or whatever money-only rule the deal-object area sets — fixed and documented, because when a treasury is short the order decides who gets paid). Ledger entries are appended in the same walk order so Ledger.seq is reproducible too. Tick order inside: (a) settle active deals, (b) countdown warnings at `deal.warnAt`, (c) expiry → renew in place if autoRenew and both parties exist and Recognition.canTrade, else push to `pending` for the player's deals or end for AI–AI, (d) expire open offers past `deal.offerExpiryTurns`, (e) end deals whose party is gone or whose parties merged into one (Game.mergeInto game.js:1010-1016), (f) trim `ended`. Placement: inside advanceTurn's Game.batch immediately BEFORE Game.tickTreasuries() (world.js:1215) and therefore before the single Market.update (:1216) and the turn increment (:1220); reads World.getTurn() as the turn being closed, the same number every other phase in the batch uses. Unconditional — not gated by Complexity (complexity.js:20-21).

serialize() → `{ v: 1, seq, deals: [...], offers: [...], pending: [...], ended: [...] }` — plain JSON only: integers for turns, no -Infinity (game.js:1666-1668 shows the trap), no undefined, no typed arrays; the statedoc round-trip test (saves.test.js:255-271) demands byte-identity after JSON. Each deal record stores everything tick reads and nothing derived: id, seller, buyer, resource (sector index), volume, price, duration, since, expires, autoRenew, offerId; offers additionally from, to, made, expires, counterOf. loadState(snap): reset(); if !snap return; copy arrays; sort by numeric id (a hand-edited save); drop deals/offers naming a nation Game.getNation cannot find (events.js:328, pacts.js:176 precedent); drop pending ids with no live deal; seq = Math.max(snap.seq || 0, highest id present). The module-level `v: 1` lets A2's transit instrument or a later shape change migrate inside Deals without touching the document VERSION.

assemble(): add `deals: Deals.serialize()` after `pacts:` (:94). applyModel(): add `Deals.loadState(doc.deals)` after `Pacts.loadState(doc.pacts)` (:183) — after Game.loadState (:178) because pruning needs Game.getNation, before World.begin (:191). STATEFUL_MODULES (:197): append 'Deals'. The nothing-forgotten test hard-codes its module map (saves.test.js:277) and its key list (:285): add `Deals` and 'deals' or the test fails with 'names Deals, which does not exist'.

steps.step: VERSION stays 3 — an old save loads
steps.detail: Do not bump. validate() refuses every v<VERSION document (:127-137); a bump to 4 would refuse Aaron's live data/state.json (rewritten every turn boundary, saves.js:222-231) and every playtester's autosave on the first reload after A1 lands, and the only 'migration' any of them needs is 'no deals' — which `Deals.loadState(undefined)` → reset() gives for free, and which is exactly true of a game saved before deals existed. No value is invented, so the v1/v2 refusal rule (:24-28, :34-51: refuse when loading means inventing values) does not apply. Every additive field since v3 was handled this way without a bump: `complexity` (:169 'a document with no complexity field predates this mode and was Full'), power stocks (:186-192), `home` (game.js:1680-1687), `player` (game.js:1794), Events.pending (events.js:326-329). The reverse case — a post-A1 document opened by a pre-A1 build — silently drops deals because applyModel ignores unknown keys; it is not a live case (main is a built copy that only moves forward, tags never move, CLAUDE.md:53-62) and is recorded as a risk, not a reason to refuse. saves.js:421's 'old format' badge is unchanged.

Add `Deals.reset()` beside `Pacts.reset()` at each of the three sites, so a new game, a Sim run and every test boot start with an empty deal ledger and seq=0 — the same singleton-reset dance every other module does (world-fixture.js:4-11).

Deals.tick takes `(tune, rng)` explicitly (events.js:288 shape). Any draw — AI acceptance of a renewal, an A4 counter-offer — comes from `rng.stream('deals')` only, never from 'ai' (ai.js:619) or the world streams, so adding deal decisions cannot reorder existing AI choices, crises or drift. Zero draws when there is nothing to decide: an empty ledger must not touch the stream, so the 866-test baseline and every pinned seed outcome are unaffected, and the stream is created lazily by rng.js:93-99 only when first used.

`pending` is the list of the player's deals that expired without autoRenew this turn (id order). `Deals.waiting()` returns it; `Deals.answer(id, decision)` clears one entry. completeTurn adds one more halt after the Events check at shell.js:250: `if (typeof Deals !== 'undefined' && Deals.waiting().length && showRenegotiate()) return true;` — the UI area builds showRenegotiate; fastForward (shell.js:266-275) then stops on it for free. Because `pending` is in the document (step 4), closing the tab mid-prompt and reopening restores the prompt; loadState drops entries whose deal is gone.

Add 'deal' to Ledger.KINDS (ai.test.js:253 asserts every kind is known) with a `what` field: signed|renewed|warn|expired|lapsed|declined|party-gone, `deal` id, `partner`, and `delta` = turns remaining for warn entries. Add 'deal' to the journal's 'world' family (journal.js:68) so 'All' stays the sum of the families (journal.js:55-61). Entries written from the tick use a non-'action' phase (propose phase 'deals') so Telemetry.collect().actions (telemetry.js:202-204) still means 'what the player chose'; signing via Moves.resolve keeps phase 'action' (moves.js:70) and so appears there automatically. Settlement is SILENT in the ledger — no entry per deal per turn — because ledger.cap is 5000 (ledger.js:84-85), the live-document quota trim keeps only recent ledger turns (saves.js:269-274), and 50 AI deals × 100 turns would push every real headline out.

Add, each with label, group 'Trade' and a doc over 20 chars naming it a placeholder (tests/tunables.test.js:10-12): `deal.durations` kind 'array' v [2,4,8,20]; `deal.warnAt` kind 'array' v [4,2,1]; `deal.offerExpiryTurns` v 2 min 1 max 20 step 1; `deal.offerCapPerTurn` v 3 min 0 max 20 step 1. The cap is enforced on insert in Deals.offer in A1 (per recipient, per turn, counting offers with `made === turn`) so the slider is live now rather than dead until A4 — game.js:1110 records why a slider that does nothing is worse than none. No history-window tunable: reuse `nation.historyWindow` as pacts.js:178-180 does. Model code reads every one through tune.get — no literal 2/4/8/20 or 4/2/1 anywhere in js/deals.js.

collect(): add `deals: Deals.serialize()` beside `ledger` (the whole section is small — ~150 bytes a deal) and bump the export `v` 1→2 (additive; a reader of v1 still parses it). sample(): add `deals` (active count) and `offers` (open count) as integers beside `nations` (:105), so 'do deal expiries create useful pressure' (addendum §3 q4) is answerable turn by turn. UI handlers call Telemetry.note with kinds 'deal-offer', 'deal-counter', 'deal-decline', 'deal-accept', 'deal-renew', 'deal-lapse' and a detail of {d: dealId} — no free text (telemetry.js:59-62). Sim.sample adds `deals: Deals.count()` and `dealsSigned: Ledger.ofKind('deal').filter(what==='signed').length` so the spec's 60-turn inter-AI check (economy-system-spec.md:591) is a series column; summarise() picks up the last row.

steps.step: Move/tunable plumbing the deal-object area must honour for determinism
steps.detail: New intents (offer, accept, counter, decline) go through Moves.plan/resolve like every other move so both callers create deals in TurnSystem order; `plan` stays pure (moves.js:1233) — it must not allocate an id; only `resolve` calls Deals.offer/accept. Signing and renewing call markTraded (moves.js:377-380) and Relations.record 'traded' (moves.js:452-453) exactly as resolveTrade does, so Influence reach (power.js:906-912) and standing are unchanged.

newTunables: deal.durations — kind 'array', v [2,4,8,20], group Trade, label 'Deal durations (turns)', doc: the menu of terms a deal may run for, in world turns (a quarter each, D163); placeholder per Addendum A §5.

deal.warnAt — kind 'array', v [4,2,1], group Trade, label 'Renegotiation countdown (turns before expiry)', doc: the remaining-turn marks at which an active deal writes a warning to the ledger and the deal ledger highlights it; placeholder.
deal.offerExpiryTurns — v 2, min 1, max 20, step 1, group Trade, label 'Open offer expiry (turns)', doc: turns an unanswered offer stays on the table before it lapses; placeholder.

deal.offerCapPerTurn — v 3, min 0, max 20, step 1, group Trade, label 'Incoming offers per turn', doc: most offers one nation can receive in a turn (Addendum A §6.2 says 3); enforced on insert in A1 so the slider is live, A4 is who fills it.
scopeCheck: No step touches demand, supply or the price index. Settlement is treasury-only (Game.earn/Game.spend, game.js:1626-1641) and Deals.tick never calls Market.update; the turn's single Market.update stays where it is (world.js:1216) and cannot see deals because it reads only Area GDP and population (market.js:42-47, :58-74). Offer pricing reads Market.getPrices()/nationSurplus the way planTrade already does (moves.js:334-335) — reads, not writes. The one nearby hazard, carrying resolveTrade's per-deal Market.update (moves.js:455) into the per-turn tick, is excluded by name in the retire list: it would reset `prev` (market.js:70) per settlement without moving prices. Not a blocker.
determinism: Ids: a single monotonic `seq` serialized with the module (ledger.js:200-205 pattern), issued only from Moves.resolve paths and Deals.tick, both of which execute in the seeded TurnSystem order (turns.js:25-31 'turnorder' stream) — so two runs on one seed produce the same 'o1, d2, ...' sequence, and a save resumes it. Order: `deals`/`offers`/`pending` are arrays kept ascending by id and written in that order; every pass walks ascending id with a fixed per-deal op order, and the tick runs in one fixed slot (before tickTreasuries, world.js:1215) so treasury float sums accumulate in one order and come out byte-identical (fingerprint() compares treasuries at world-fixture.js:211). Ledger entries are appended in walk order so Ledger.seq and entry ids match across runs. Randomness: only `rng.stream('deals')`, and no draw when idle, so the existing streams (ai, combat, drift, events, leaders, names, recognition, scenario, spawn, turnorder, unite) never shift and every pinned-seed test keeps its answer; rng.serialize() (rng.js:102-106) already writes every touched stream, so the 'deals' stream survives a save. No Date.now/Math.random (rng.js:131-134 is the only permitted site). Object keyed by nation id is banned in this module because integer-like keys enumerate first. Player-driven runs are not replayable by definition; headless runs through AI.round (ai.js:711-732) are, and that is what the tests pin.
risks: Ledger bloat: if the deal-object area logs settlement per deal per turn, ledger.cap (5000, ledger.js:84-85) and the live-document quota trim (saves.js:269-274) start discarding real news within ~100 turns of a 50-deal world. Mitigated by making settlement silent in the ledger; the deal ledger UI is where settlement is read.

A post-A1 document opened in a pre-A1 build loads and silently drops its deals (applyModel ignores unknown keys; the build stamp only compares Area counts, statedoc.js:62-68). Not a live case today (main only moves forward), recorded rather than guarded.

Party death and union: Game.mergeInto (game.js:1010-1016) and pruneEmpty (:1070-1076) remove nations without telling anyone; a deal whose party is gone must be ended by the tick's prune pass (reason 'party-gone'), and a deal whose two parties united into one nation becomes a self-deal that must also end. Successor-state inheritance is spec Phase 7 (treaty succession) and is NOT built — old deals simply end.

Renegotiation prompt after a load: SaveManager.apply (saves.js:105-112) sweeps the AI and selects the player but never calls completeTurn, so a restored `pending` list is only shown at the next End turn unless the UI area re-raises it on load — the same gap Events.pending has today (unverified, see below).

Float determinism depends on the tick slot never moving: if a later stage inserts a treasury-touching pass between Deals.tick and tickTreasuries, sums change in the last bit and byte-identity across builds (not across runs) breaks — acceptable, but document the slot in DESIGN.md.

The 'deals' rng stream is the guard against perturbing the AI; if A4 draws counter-offer decisions from the 'ai' stream instead (ai.js:619), every existing AI choice after the first deal reorders. Name the stream in DESIGN.md now so A4 inherits it.

Telemetry and Journal are not loaded by tests/run.html (:85-116) and no test references them, so their deal wiring can only be verified in the browser; keep the changes to collect()/sample()/FAMILIES trivially small.

tradeCooldown keys stay integer-like nation ids in a plain object (game.js:1055); enumeration order there is only used for counting (power.js:912) so it is safe, but nobody should iterate it to drive deal logic.
Save size grows by ~150 bytes per deal and offer — negligible against a 670 KB turn-3 document (saves.js:242-247).
tests: tests/saves.test.js 'enumerates every stateful module': add Deals to the hard-coded `mods` map (:277) and 'deals' to the key list (:285), so STATEFUL_MODULES naming 'Deals' is checked against a real serialize/loadState pair and the document actually carries the section.

Deals: serialize → loadState → serialize is the identity (JSON.stringify equal) for a state holding two active deals, one open offer, one pending renegotiation and one ended record, after a JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()) round trip.

A version-3 document with no `deals` key validates (StateDoc.validate returns null) and applies, leaving Deals.count() at 0 and the rest of the world identical — the pin that an old save loads rather than being refused.

Extend 'a full snapshot -> apply reproduces the whole world' (saves.test.js:104): sign a deal through Moves.resolve before the snapshot and assert Deals.serialize() deepEquals its pre-scribble value after applyModel.

Extend 'a restored world advances identically to one that never saved' (saves.test.js:120): with a 4-turn deal in flight, save at turn 4, play 6 rounds via AI.round both ways, and assert fingerprint() and Deals.serialize() (including `ended`) are deepEqual.
Same seed ⇒ same deal ledger: two fresh bootWorld({seed}) runs of N AI.round each yield identical Deals.serialize() and identical Ledger.ofKind('deal') entries (ids, order, since/expires).
Ids are monotonic, prefixed and unforgeable: two offers are 'o1' and 'o2', accepting one yields 'd3', a caller-supplied id is overwritten, and after loadState({seq: 7}) the next id is 'o8'.

Iteration is by id, not by key order: create deals between '48', '06' and a founded 'n…' nation in scrambled order, assert the settlement walk order is ascending id, and that two identical worlds end the tick with treasuries equal under Object.is (bit-identical), not merely close().

An idle tick draws nothing: with no deals or offers, rng.totalDraws() is unchanged across Deals.tick; with deals, only the 'deals' stream's count moves and every other stream's count is unchanged (rng.serialize().streams before vs after).

Countdown and expiry reproduce across a save: a 4-turn deal produces exactly one 'warn' entry at each `deal.warnAt` threshold and one 'expired'/'renewed' entry at expiry; saving mid-countdown and reloading yields the same entries with no duplicate and none missed.

A dead party ends the deal: after Game.mergeInto absorbs one party the next tick records reason 'party-gone', and loadState of a document naming a nation that no longer exists drops that deal and its pending entry (events.js:328 pattern).

Deal signing keeps the old bookkeeping: after Moves.resolve of a deal-signing intent, both nations' tradeCooldown[partner] equals World.getTurn() and Relations records 'traded' in both directions — so power.js's trade-reach term and standing are unchanged by A1.

Offer cap and expiry are live tunables: with `deal.offerCapPerTurn` set to 1 on a cloned tune a second offer to the same recipient in one turn is refused; an offer older than `deal.offerExpiryTurns` lapses on the tick with an 'ended' record.

tests/tunables.test.js already checks label/group/doc for every SCHEMA key (:10-12); add one assertion that `deal.durations` and `deal.warnAt` are kind 'array' and read back unchanged through createTune().get.

Ledger vocabulary: Ledger.KINDS includes 'deal' (scenario.test.js:134 pattern), and a 30-round AI run produces no entry whose kind is unknown (ai.test.js:253 already covers this once 'deal' is in KINDS).

Sim.sample carries `deals` and `dealsSigned`, and a 60-round Sim.run({ai: true}) ends with dealsSigned > 0 once the AI can propose (A4) — write it now as it.skip with the A4 note, so the spec's inter-AI verification (spec:591) has a home.
unverified: Whether any consumer other than Telemetry.collect (:202-204) switches on ledger `phase`; I grepped the writers (phase: 'action'|'roster'|'secession') but not every reader, so 'deals' as a new phase value is proposed, not confirmed safe.
How a pending Events crisis is re-shown after SaveManager.apply without an End turn (saves.js:105-112 does not call completeTurn); the renegotiation prompt inherits whatever that behaviour is.
The test count: the handoff says 861 green (docs/handoffs/2026-09-05_0200:3), the task says 866; I did not run the suite (read-only brief).
Whether tunables.test checks min/max/step on array-kind entries — :10-12 shows only label/group/doc; the groups()-coverage test at :112-116 will include new keys automatically.
Whether anything outside the repo parses the telemetry export's `v` (telemetry.js:176); the bump to 2 is additive either way.

The exact deal record fields (seller/buyer roles, price basis, what money-only settlement pays whom) belong to the deal-object area; the persistence rules above hold for any record shape that is plain JSON and carries everything the tick reads.
Whether a journal test pins 'All is the sum of the families' — no test file references Journal or FAMILIES, so adding 'deal' to the 'world' family is verified only by reading journal.js:55-69.
